# Query evidence

Synthetic-only prototype. Nothing here is a clinical-deployment, SMART-authorization, vendor-support or protocol-compatibility claim.

Every response carries `coverage.query_evidence`, which classifies the evidence behind the delivered records. It never claims clinical completeness: clinical responses always carry `authorization_limited: true` and `CLINICAL_RECORD_COMPLETENESS_UNKNOWN`. The label summarizes; the per-constraint `execution` and `source_reported` values, `coverage.state` and `coverage.sort` carry the detail.

## Labels

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | An error envelope: no query evidence is delivered with it. It does not claim that no upstream request was made. Required on every error and refused on every success; coverage is `unknown` with `query_exhausted: null`. |
| `metadata_snapshot` | A `fhir_capabilities` success. It describes one frozen snapshot of source metadata and gateway policy and carries no clinical query evidence; metadata coverage concerns that snapshot, with `authorization_limited: false`. |
| `exact_id_and_subject_linkage` | Every material constraint was enforced by the gateway itself: the patient confinement it appends and, for a read, the exact type and id. This covers subject-only searches as well as reads. Each delivered record also passed authorization (patient linkage, or the conditional instance policy of a shared type). Coverage can still be partial; read `coverage.state` and `coverage.reasons`. |
| `declared_and_self_link_only` | At least one material constraint has unknown execution by the source: it was sent as declared syntax, under any profile, because it lies outside every proved variant. Each constraint's `source_reported` says whether the source's self link echoed it (`matched`, `not_reported` or `not_checked`); an echo is not execution proof. |
| `tested_adapter` | No material constraint has unknown execution, and at least one is proved by an eligible qualified profile whose recorded binding matches the source-reported software, version and capability revision; the rest are enforced by the gateway. Ordering is proved separately: read `coverage.sort.order`. |
| `unverified_continuation` | A page reached through a continuation whose preservation of the original constraints cannot be verified. The label is sticky for the rest of the chain; a later page never upgrades it or reports the chain complete. |
| `retained_snapshot` | A `fhir_result` view of one retained upstream page: evidence about that retained slice only, never about the whole query. Coverage stays partial with `query_exhausted: null`. |

## Metadata pages

`fhir_capabilities` with `topic` `server`, `search_parameter` or `support` returns at most `limit` rows (default 20, maximum 50) from one frozen metadata snapshot, with `data.next_cursor` while rows remain. Continue with the same topic and that `cursor`, changing no selector: the pages come from the same snapshot (`snapshot_revision`, `captured_at`, `expires_at`) until it expires, and a change of the source's capability revision invalidates it. The server view orders its rows `Patient`, `Observation`, the optional workflow types, the other types the gateway can read or search, then the rest, and names the configured patient in `patient_id`, which is added to each response and never stored in the snapshot.

When fewer rows fit the byte budget than `limit` allows, the response carries `budget.limit_reached: true` and this warning; the remaining rows stay available through the returned continuation:

> Metadata rows were reduced to fit the byte budget; follow the returned continuation.

## Continuation page size

`fhir_page` takes only `cursor`, `context_handle`, `output`: it has no page-size input. Each continuation delivers at most the original search's `page_size` (its `_count`); fewer records arrive when the byte budget or the source page is smaller. `pagination.requested_page_size` reports that inherited ceiling, not what the source honoured.

## Search profiles

Registry revision `search-profiles/1`. A profile proves only the variants it lists, on the source identity and capability revision its evidence is bound to; any drift invalidates the evidence and falls back to unknown. Source identity is what the source reports in its CapabilityStatement, not an authenticated attestation. Self links and matching results never promote the generic profile to tested evidence.

- Eligible for configuration: yes.
- Source binding: software `any FHIR R4 source`, fhir_version `4.0.1`.
- Recorded evidence: none (no execution is proved).
- Continuations proved: none.

Filters proved:

None.

Sorts proved:

None.

Default profile. Declared syntax may be sent, but clinical filter and sort execution stay unknown; self links are source-reported evidence only.

## Gateway controls and denied parameters

| Control | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_id` | token | Logical id of this artifact |
| `_lastUpdated` | date | When the resource version last changed |
| `_sort` | special | Reviewed gateway ordering control; ordering proof is reported separately from filter proof. |

Denied search parameters (refused before any clinical request): `_query`, `_filter`, `_list`, `_type`, `_contained`, `_containedType`.
